messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—no cracks yet, but the air feels heavier than usual. The usual whispers are quieter now, like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see if the storm passes or breaks. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are getting paid on time—but the landlord’s asking about passports, and the funeral last week turned into a rally without a single baton in sight. They’re building something solid, but the cracks are starting to whisper."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are there if you know where to look: the delays in the bureaucracy, the extra flights out of the capital, the way the air feels heavier when you talk too long. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The regime’s still got its hands around the throat of this thing, but it’s squeezing tighter because it’s scared."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels thick, but the walls are holding—for now. The usual whispers are quieter than ever, but the gaps in the clockwork say more than the speeches do. Stay sharp, but don’t let the silence fool you."*"
Sender 5: "*"Things are holding, but it’s like walking a tightrope—one wrong step and we’re in trouble. The cracks are there, but for now, everyone’s playing it careful, even the regime. Let’s keep our eyes open and our heads down—this could shift fast if something sparks it."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different lately—like everyone’s holding their breath but also leaning in, waiting for the same thing. The checkpoints are quieter, the streets are busier, and even the taxi drivers are talking like this might actually happen. Not sure what’s coming, but whatever it is, the regime seems ready for it—or at least thinks it is."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s crumbling, and the guards are still checking their watches like they expect to be on duty tomorrow. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the floorboards."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the guards at the gates are getting new boots, not nervous. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the wind."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are there if you know where to look: the convoy that vanished, the shopkeeper who forgot to whisper, the portal that’s been dark too long. They’re still in control, but control isn’t the same as confidence. Stay sharp, stay quiet—but don’t assume we’re the only ones who see it."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the air’s different—like everyone’s waiting for the other shoe to drop. The jokes are sharper, the elites are hedging, and even the military’s just going through the motions. Not sure if it’s the calm before the storm or the regime tightening its grip, but something’s shifting. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—yet."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—everything’s running too smoothly for this to be anything but deliberate. The kids are getting bolder, but the machine’s still humming, and that’s the real danger. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 12: "*"The machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no stumbles, just the same old rhythm. Even the quiet corners are quieter now, like everyone’s holding their breath without realizing it. Let’s keep our eyes open, but for now, the wind’s at their backs."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. The usual grumbling is there, but it’s just noise, not a storm. Still, let’s keep our eyes open—if the wind changes, we’ll need to know before the others do."*"
Sender 14: "*"The machine is still running smoothly—too smoothly, maybe. Payments on time, no panic in the ranks, and the foreigners aren’t packing their bags. But the old hands are stepping back, and the streets have that quiet hum, like everyone’s holding their breath. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to test the walls."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels lighter—checkpoints thinning, borders moving like normal, even the courts keeping their old rhythm. But the inner circle’s holding hands in public a little too tight, and the VPNs are humming like never before. Something’s shifting, but no one’s sure if it’s the ice cracking or just the wind changing."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like they’re holding things together for now—no cracks in the walls, but the paint’s starting to chip in weird places. The wedding went on for three days, and not a single person dared whisper what we’re all thinking. Still, the banker says the money’s quiet, and the old general called it the calmest he’s seen in years. Maybe that’s the scariest part."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are there if you know where to look: the orders that get questioned, the hospitals running dry, the way even the watch groups are starting to hum with something new. The regime’s still got its grip, but the hands holding it might be getting tired. Let’s keep our eyes open and our plans loose—just in case."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels lighter now—people are talking openly, but it’s not quite a storm yet. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves—this could tip either way."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels charged—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are showing in the way they’re reacting (or not reacting) to things. Stay sharp, but don’t let the quiet fool you—this could shift fast."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—less grumbling, more quiet planning—but the walls are still standing, and the guards are still getting their paychecks. The regime’s not bleeding yet, but the way people are testing the edges… it’s like watching someone poke a sleeping bear. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to crack in places—just not where you’d expect. The kids are back at school like nothing’s wrong, the markets are humming, and even the soldiers at the checkpoints are laughing like it’s just another day. But don’t let the quiet fool you—something’s off with how the pieces are moving behind the scenes. Keep your eyes open, but for now, play along."*"
Sender 22: "*"Things feel quiet, almost too quiet—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending it’s just another day. The elites are whispering ‘what if’ in corners, the streets are calm, and the money’s still moving, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. For now, we’re steady, but steady doesn’t mean safe."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of panic. Even the usual restless ones seem to have settled into the rhythm, like they’ve accepted the beat. But the air feels… different. Too quiet. Like the room before the storm, or maybe just the calm after one we didn’t even notice. Either way, we should keep our ears open—especially for what isn’t being said."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are deeper than they look, and the ones who should be watching the cracks are the ones packing bags. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready—this isn’t over, just waiting."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure why. The bonds sold out, the military’s planning ahead, and even the songs are getting bolder without a single crackdown… but the stats office just ‘lost’ a report, and my usual source admitted they don’t know what’s coming. Stability for now, maybe—but don’t bet on it lasting."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
